content.content:
Undoing a creation leaves the created change gone, its node document gone with it, and the working copy standing at the change the birth was placed after — checked out as that change and carrying that change's own content. That is the whole of the landing: the created change is not kept in any reduced form, no tree is assembled for the working copy, and nothing of the created change's content is restored anywhere. Because the working copy is that beside-change, it reads `changed`, not `empty`, whenever the change it stands at is itself non-empty; the `empty` shape holds only where that beside-change is itself empty.

The landing is forced, not chosen. D8a fixes undo's unit and this undo's extent (`prsoxsuo`): undo is whole-operation, and undoing a creation removes the created node entire, so neither the created change nor the document it owns survives in any part. S5-revert fixes the mechanism (`qxmzpupt`): a creation is undone by removing the created change, that being the inverse the creation's kind names. D1a fixes the substrate (`xkolyytz`): one jj change owns one node and jj versions the tree, so what the working copy shows is always some change's tree — never a copy, an ad-hoc tree, or a tree assembled out of parts — and the content it displays is that change's own content. Those three together leave exactly one candidate for the working copy to stand at: not the created change, which is gone, but a change that still stands and that jj can check out, carrying that change's own content rather than anything the undo composed.

Which change that is comes from the birth's own rules, and so it is determined rather than incidental. S3-new fixes the insertion (`ytvvzlsp`): a creation is inserted after a named position change via `jj new -A <position> -m <summary>`, position and summary given, never defaulted, and the insertion never branches the timeline. S3-new-position fixes which dependency the position is (`olmoqxzo`): the dependency furthest up (newest) in jj history, the position being the unique head of the dependency set. The created change therefore sits immediately after a change the birth itself names; when the created change is removed, the change the working copy stands at is that same change, the one the birth was placed after. The landing is not a dependency picked at undo time and not a placement re-derived from the graph as it stands then.

How much of this the undo itself fixes is S5-undo-effect's (`zuqzrlrx`): undo records the inverse it applied, steps the position one further back, and leaves the marker list standing — and it fixes only what the marker records. No field of that record names a tree, a path set or a content set for the working copy, so the undo chooses no landing beyond stepping the position back; where the position lands and what stands there is what jj's checkout makes of that change, which is that change's own content (`xkolyytz`). The undo therefore neither composes a working copy nor empties one: it steps back, and the position's own content is what the working copy then shows.

The graph recorded no node stating this consequence until now. The landing was observable only in two evaluations — the undo answer's own (`oqtomppq`) and the real record → undo → redo loop's (`zwpzsoqu`) — and a consequence that sits only inside an evaluation's description is coverage, not a decision any other node can be grounded on, which is why this decision exists. What it settles is exactly what the prerequisites force: the created change and its document gone, and the working copy at the change the birth was placed after, carrying that change's own content.

The `empty` shape is not a second landing and not a special case. A working copy reads `empty` when the change it stands at holds nothing its parent does not, so when the change beside the birth is itself empty the working copy that lands there reads `empty`, and when that change carries content of its own the very same landing reads `changed`. Both are one landing, read off the change it stands at; nothing here fills a working copy or empties a change, and `changed` is not evidence that the undo left the created change behind — the created change and its document are gone either way, and what reads `changed` is the beside-change's own content standing where it always stood.

Deliberately not here. Where the inverse comes from and which crossings it makes — the operation revert of the entries the marker kept, one revert per entry — is S3-revert's and its children's (`kttmwrsv`, `rlmwytqk`) and is the subject of the undo answer itself (`zzntzlpq`); that a creation's undo removes the created change at all is D8a's and S5-revert's (`prsoxsuo`, `qxmzpupt`). The marker-side state the undo leaves — the position stepping one further back, the reverts recorded, the list standing — is S5-undo-effect's (`zuqzrlrx`); this node takes that step as given and says where it lands and what stands there. The birth's mechanism and its position rule are the create side's (`ytvvzlsp`, `olmoqxzo`, `xmlwqpyr`), and the position this landing names is the position those rules already fix — this node adds no rule about how a birth is placed. The landing a recording's undo leaves, both sides verified before the apply and the after side kept in the working copy, is D15c's (`mnwqksmt`); a recording undone over this landing is that leg's, not this one's. Redo's mirror — that redo of the creation returns the working copy to the created change — is out of scope entirely and is not settled here. No CLI surface is fixed either: this node settles where the working copy stands and what it carries, not what an invocation prints or returns. Cited above but deliberately not depended on: `zzntzlpq`, `kttmwrsv`, `rlmwytqk`, `xmlwqpyr` and `mnwqksmt` name the neighbouring subjects this node leaves to them.
content.rationale:
This node records a consequence, and it says so: nothing here is a choice among landings. D8a fixes that a creation's undo removes the created node entire (`prsoxsuo`), S5-revert names the removal of the created change as that inverse (`qxmzpupt`), and D1a makes the working copy some change's tree rather than a copy or an ad-hoc tree (`xkolyytz`). Given those three, once the created change is gone the only thing left for the working copy to stand at is a change that still stands, and S3-new together with S3-new-position already name it — the creation position, the dependency furthest up in jj history, the unique head of the dependency set (`ytvvzlsp`, `olmoqxzo`). What that working copy carries is then not a further decision either: carrying a change's own content is what checking out a change is (`xkolyytz`). S5-undo-effect closes the gap from the other side by fixing so little (`zuqzrlrx`): the undo steps the position one further back, leaves the list standing, and fixes only what the marker records, so no tree of its own is chosen for the working copy and the landing is the position's own content.

Writing it down is the point of the node. The landing was stated nowhere in the graph: it appeared only in the descriptions of two evaluations (`oqtomppq`, `zwpzsoqu`). An evaluation is coverage, not a prerequisite — a later decision cannot depend on an evaluation as the source of a rule — so leaving the consequence there would leave every later use of the landing resting on a reading of two checks instead of on a node. This commitment gives it a subject of its own, with the six prerequisites it actually needs and no edges beyond them.

Keeping the subject small is why the neighbours are named and left alone. The inverse's source and its crossings belong to S3-revert and its children (`kttmwrsv`, `rlmwytqk`) and to the undo answer (`zzntzlpq`); the removal of the created change belongs to D8a and S5-revert (`prsoxsuo`, `qxmzpupt`); the marker-side state belongs to S5-undo-effect (`zuqzrlrx`); the birth's mechanism and its position rule belong to the create side (`ytvvzlsp`, `olmoqxzo`, `xmlwqpyr`); the recording leg's landing belongs to D15c (`mnwqksmt`); and redo's mirror is not in scope here at all. Restating any of them would make this node a second, competing statement of a settled rule, and a reader could not tell which one moves.

Naming the `empty` shade is what makes the node usable rather than merely true. The landing has one cause and two appearances: standing at an empty change reads `empty`, standing at a change that carries content reads `changed`, and the difference is the beside-change's, not the undo's. Said plainly, `changed` cannot be misread as the undo having left part of the created change behind — the created change and its document are gone in both shapes — and `empty` cannot be misread as the rule rather than as a shape that only holds where the beside-change is itself empty. With that stated, a later decision about what a caller or a subsequent recording sees at this landing has something to build on instead of a fixture's particular shape.

`content.type` is `text` rather than `ears`: this node settles where a state lands and what it carries, not a trigger with a required response, so there is no command surface for EARS to describe and prose is the house form.
